verse.speaker: Arjuna
verse.setting: Arjuna confesses the mind is as hard to hold as the wind; Krishna answers.
verse.sanskrit: चञ्चलं हि मनः कृष्ण प्रमाथि बलवद्दृढम् । तस्याहं निग्रहं मन्ये वायोरिव सुदुष्करम् ॥
verse.line: The mind is restless, stormy, stubborn and strong. Holding it feels like holding the wind.
verse.translation: For the mind is restless, Krishna, turbulent, powerful and stubborn. I think it is as hard to hold as the wind.
verse.why: The mind is hard to hold, but practice and letting go train it.

prasang.summary: Arjuna says the mind is restless, stormy and stubborn. Krishna agrees, and says practice and letting go can train it.
prasang.lesson: The mind is hard to hold, but practice and letting go train it.

verse.meaning: Arjuna, exhausted on the battlefield of his own thoughts, tells Krishna that the mind is as hard to hold as the wind. It is restless, turbulent and stubborn. Krishna agrees without surprise. He says this is the nature of the mind, but it can be trained through practice and by letting go of attachment to the results of your efforts.
verse.for_you: Your mind feels like it is running on seven hours of phone time and nothing else. It is not broken. It is just restless, like Arjuna said. The practice is not to stop it, but to give it one place to land right now.

prasang.title: Nidagha's lament
prasang.summary: Young Nidagha returns from pilgrimage disillusioned and pours out his heart to his teacher Ribhu: life is fleeting, the mind runs like a stray dog, craving gnaws every good quality, and mastering the mind is harder than drinking the ocean.
prasang.lesson: Naming how restless your mind is, is where peace begins.

verse.meaning: Nidagha comes back from a long pilgrimage. Their heart is heavy and they sit down with their teacher Ribhu. They tell Ribhu that life feels like it is slipping away. Their mind keeps running around like a stray dog, looking for scraps. Every good thing they try to do gets eaten away by craving. They say that trying to master this mind feels harder than drinking the whole ocean in one go. Ribhu listens and then says that the first step to quiet is to simply see this pattern.
verse.for_you: Your mind has been running for hours, and it does not stop because it is hungry. It wants the phone, it wants a distraction. Today, sit with it without fighting. See that the restlessness is just a dog looking for a place to rest.

verse.line: A churned-up lake settles and clears on its own. So does a mind, given time.
verse.translation: A great lake that has been churned up settles and clears by itself. In the same way a person who has gained wisdom becomes clear by himself.
verse.why: Grief can't restore what's gone. Want what's within reach, and let others' success be.

verse.speaker: Bhartrihari
verse.sanskrit: परिभ्रमसि किं मुधा क्वचन चित्त विश्राम्यतां स्वयं भवति यद्यथा भवति तत्तथा नान्यथा । अतीतमननुस्मरन्नपि च भाव्यसंकल्पयन् नतर्कितसमागमाननुभवामि भोगानहम् ॥
verse.line: Why wander, mind? Rest. Not replaying the past, not scripting the future, I take what comes.
verse.translation: Why do you wander about in vain, mind? Rest somewhere. Whatever is to happen happens just as it will, and not otherwise. Not recalling the past, not planning the future, I enjoy the pleasures that come to me unlooked-for.
verse.why: Stop seeking approval and rehearsing outcomes; the calm you want is already inside.
verse.misuse: Not an argument against planning; it is for the worry loop once you have done your part.

story.title: King Janaka overhears the sages and keeps ruling, with a free mind
story.story_hook: One spring morning, a king out for a walk overheard a song that he could not stop thinking about.
story.summary: Walking in his spring garden, King Janaka overhears hidden sages singing about the self. Shaken, he climbs to his palace roof and questions everything he has lived for. When his doorkeeper calls him to the day's work, he decides not to run away: he gets up and does his duties, but with a mind that no longer clutches.
story.lesson: You don't have to leave your life to change it. Do the day's work with a mind that doesn't clutch.

anchor.speaker: Janaka
anchor.setting: King Janaka, alone on his palace roof after overhearing wandering sages, rethinks his life.
anchor.sanskrit: संपदश्च विचित्रा यास्ताश्चेच्चित्तेन संमताः । तत्ता अपि महारम्भा हन्त मन्ये महापदः ॥ आपदोऽपि विचित्रा यास्ताश्चेन्मनसि संमताः । तत्ता अपि महारम्भा मन्ये मनसि संपदः ॥
anchor.line: Good fortune the mind clutches becomes trouble. Trouble the mind accepts becomes a kind of fortune.
anchor.translation: All those dazzling fortunes, if the mind clings to them, are really great calamities in grand disguise. And all those varied misfortunes, if the mind accepts them, are really fortunes.
anchor.why: You don't have to leave your life to change it. Do the day's work with a mind that doesn't clutch.
anchor.misuse: Accepting a hardship doesn't mean not fixing what can be fixed.

weeks.title: The mind that will not settle

script: Your mind will not settle right now. You sit with your books, and the thoughts just scatter. Seven hours on the phone has taught your mind to run. It is exhausting. It is not broken. It is just restless.

On the battlefield, Arjuna is exhausted. He has asked Krishna what is right. Krishna has just told him to act. Arjuna says no, my mind is too hard to hold. It is like the wind. And Krishna replies: And Arjuna said:
चञ्चलं हि मनः कृष्ण प्रमाथि बलवद्दृढम्, तस्याहं निग्रहं मन्ये वायोरिव सुदुष्करम्.
In plain words: The mind is restless, stormy, stubborn and strong. Holding it feels like holding the wind.

Arjuna, exhausted on the battlefield of his own thoughts, tells Krishna that the mind is as hard to hold as the wind. It is restless, turbulent and stubborn. Krishna agrees without surprise. He says this is the nature of the mind, but it can be trained through practice and by letting go of attachment to the results of your efforts.

Right now, close the phone. Put it face down. Pick one thing in front of you and place your full attention there. Just for a minute. Let the mind land there. You do not need to fix the whole day. Just one place to land.
Where can your mind land for just one minute?

depth.life: You sit with your books and your phone. Seven hours a day the screen pulls your mind this way and that. It feels like you are scattered and the studying is not sticking. The restlessness is the thing that is hurting you right now.
depth.points: The mind is not a broken thing. It is a force that wants to move. It is not your fault that it is restless. It is just what a mind does until it learns one true place to rest.
depth.practice: Put the phone face down on the desk for five minutes. Let your eyes rest on one page. Do not force the thoughts away.
depth.question: What is the one thing your mind wants to rest on right now?
